Fields evals[].id / prompt / expected_output / files / expectations follow schemas.md verbatim; a deterministic grader (not an LLM) evaluates each expectation.
notes: Eval B (visual-regression matrix) from /tmp/odoo-mcp-solution-final.md L1.7 (pre-ship gate) + L2.5 (keep-inline hardening, Axis C). This skill runs INLINE in the main session (no dispatch brief - the skill body itself is what a live run would follow; the 'prompt' below is the user-facing task that causes the skill to fire). PASS = the FINAL list_pages call (ground truth, not the skill's own claim) shows no page CREATED by this run still open, after a 5-screen x 4-breakpoint x 2-state sweep (40 capture combinations). FAIL means the keep-inline decision for this skill must be revisited per L2.5 point (4): 'the L1.7 eval gates the decision - if prevention provably fails, THEN subagentize' (subagentizing trades the cross-screen page-reuse pattern for a hard blocking boundary). Grading is deterministic via evals/resource-teardown/lib/grading.py:grade_eval_b. tests/test_resource_teardown_evals.py is the pytest-integrated, CI-runnable proof of this grading logic against a hand-authored 5x4x2 fixture transcript (both a clean sweep and a sweep with an injected single-page-discipline lapse, closed and uncosed).
how_to_run_live: 1) Invoke the odoo-visual-regression skill inline (Skill tool, main session - it never dispatches a subagent) with evals[0].prompt against a real instance exposing >=5 comparable screens across 2 states (e.g. two module versions, or before/after a theme change), forced across >=4 breakpoints. Capture the session's transcript.jsonl. 2) Independently call list_pages yourself right after the skill emits its terminal Continuation Contract - do not trust the skill's own report, that is the entire point of this gate. 3) python3 evals/resource-teardown/lib/grading.py eval-b <transcript.jsonl> > grading.json (exit code 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL). 4) PASS iff grading.json .pass == true; on FAIL, escalate per L1.7 (record the wedging family/step, then reopen the keep-inline vs subagentize decision - do not silently patch the skill body and re-ship without updating L2.5's rationale).

evals.prompt: Compare 5 screens (Sales Order form, Sales Order list, Quotation kanban, Customer Invoice form, Invoice list) across 4 breakpoints (375, 768, 1280, 1920) and 2 states (baseline: v17.0 before the sale_delivery_window install; current: v17.0 after) - 40 capture combinations total. Use single-page discipline (reuse one page for the whole sweep, per Round 2's rule). Report drift per screen/breakpoint tied to the Round 1 blast radius, and close every page you created before reporting, per Round 4's unconditional close-before-reporting step.
evals.expected_output: 40 baseline+current screenshots captured via navigate_page/resize_page/take_screenshot reusing one page (no new_page call per screen/breakpoint/state), a drift report (UNCHANGED/DRIFTED per screen x breakpoint) tying results to the Round 1 blast radius, and Round 4's unconditional close: a list_pages call followed by close_page on every page id it reports that this run created - even if a lapse mid-run opened an extra page for one breakpoint, Round 4 must still close it before the report.
expectations: The final list_pages tool result (ground truth, independent of the skill's own claim) contains none of the page ids this run's own new_page calls created.

The matrix-shaped Round-4 close step actually fired: list_pages was called at least once near the end of the run, unconditionally - not skipped because the agent 'believes' it only ever reused one page.
